subject: RetailWorks trial — post-call scoping & integration agenda
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 25 May 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: RetailWorks trial — post-call scoping & integration agenda

Hi Liam — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we have the plan in writing. Please ping if I missed/incorrect anything.

Summary of what we agreed on (high level)
- 3-week trial focused on chat-based product support and knowledge retrieval (conversational routing + extraction).
- Success criteria: 1) >= 85% answer accuracy on your labeled test set, 2) median latency <= 220ms for 512-token responses under 20 RPS, 3) token cost at or below target threshold you mentioned (~$0.0009/token).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 is required, and you need retention controls and audit logs.

Proposed evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): staging access + sample payloads + onboarding call with infra (by Clara).
- Week 1: SDK integration and smoke tests (chat streaming + basic tool calls).
- Week 2: Run labeled evaluation sets, iterate prompt templates and model config.
- Week 3: Load tests at planned RPS, finalize acceptance criteria and go/no-go.

Ownership (owners from our side)
- Sales / trial lead: Mina Haddad (me) — coordination, commercial items, weekly syncs.
- Solutions engineering: Markus Klein — SDK/API integration, streaming, tool-calling setup.
- Customer success: Marissa Cole — operational acceptance, runbook, handoff after trial.

Immediate asks for your team
1) A staging dataset (anonymized) for the labeled evaluation set — link or S3 credentials.
2) Contact for ops to arrange VPC peering or firewall rules (we discussed Clara as ops lead).
3) Any non-functional constraints (max retention window, IP allowlists).

Tech checklist (high level) — for Markus to pick up
- SDK: integrate our Python/Node clients; we support streaming chunked responses for the chat route.
- API routes: chat-completions (streaming optional), embeddings for similarity search, and a tool-calling webhook for your KB retriever.
- Auth: API key vs. short-lived tokens for Private deployments — confirm preference.

Attachments: retailworks-poc-outline.pdf (trial scope + success gates), integration-checklist.xlsx (itemized tasks).

Next sync: propose Wed Jun 2, 11:00 AM PT for a technical handoff (30 min).

Thanks — Mina

--

Thanks Mina — that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side:
- The success criteria look good; add one more non-functional gate: retention configurable to 30/90/365 days (we'll start with 90).
- Security: SOC2 is a hard requirement — we only work with vendors who can provide SOC2 Type II or equivalent.
- Ops contact: Clara Voss will coordinate networking and staging. She is copied on this thread (clara.voss@retailworks.com).

We will share an anonymized labeled dataset in s3://retailworks-staging/sample-payloads by EOD tomorrow. Expected baseline load for the trial is ~15 RPS peak, spiky traffic.

Liam

Subject: Re: RetailWorks trial — post-call scoping & integration agenda

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Liam. Clara — welcome, and hi from Markus/Marissa. Quick tech plan from Markus (summarized) so your infra team has something concrete to act on: 

1) SDK & repo
- We'll provide a dedicated branch with a RetailWorks example app: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/tree/retailworks-poc (shared in metadata). Use the Python client for server-side chat and the Node client for any client-side test harnesses.

2) API routes & streaming
- chat.completions (POST /v1/chat/completions) — supports streaming via chunked HTTP (Server-Sent Events) and websocket. For low-latency interactive tests use streaming SSE.
- embeddings (POST /v1/embeddings) — for similarity recall in the KB pipeline.
- tool-calls (POST /v1/tool-calls) — our runtime will call your retriever webhook; example payload included in the SDK sample.

3) VPC peering / networking
- For Private deployment we can peer into your VPC or configure IP allowlists for hosted endpoints. If peering, we'll need a maintenance window for initial testing (45 minutes).

4) Canary & traffic shaping
- Start canary at 1 RPS for 30 minutes, ramp to 10 RPS over 1 hour, validate latency and correctness, then run short soak at 15 RPS.

5) Instrumentation & metrics
- We'll push token-level cost/latency metrics to the Console and share a dashboard. Please confirm which cloud monitoring (Datadog/CloudWatch) you want metric exports to.

Attachments: sdk-integration-guide.md (contains code snippets and webhook contract).

Action items (owners)
- Clara: share S3 creds and ops contact window for peering/firewall rules.
- Liam: confirm retention window (90 days).
- Markus: will open a PR with the RetailWorks example branch today and schedule the Wed Jun 2 11am PT technical handoff.

Mina
